utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Does that show reference to the 19 December instructions, or some instructions?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I would say that this is a reference to those instructions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And then the following paragraph goes on to say the Crisis Staff will be appointed at the inaugural session of the Assembly of the Serbian people.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown another new document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Excuse me. Let me object to authenticity of this one, Your Honour, P2686A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I didn't ask with regard to the first of these newly introduced -- I didn't ask you with regard to the first of these newly introduced documents, because the first one, 2684, bears a signature and a stamp. And basing myself on the approach that you have adopted throughout, I take it that the authenticity of that document is not being contested at this stage. Yes, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown another document. If that could be marked Exhibit P2687.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This document is a decision to proclaim the Serbian Municipal Assembly of Ilidza, dated the 3rd of January, 1992. Mr. Treanor, whilst it's not a decision setting up a Crisis Staff, does it make reference to the instructions, Variant A and B?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, since this is the first time I've set eyes on this document, to my knowledge, you might call my attention to --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In the preamble.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- The part you have in mind. Yes, yes, yes. There's reference to instructions of the Serbian Democratic Party of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Main Board, number 79, of 19 December 1991, which would certainly appear to me to be a reference to the instructions that we are discussing here. The number 79, I would take to mean the numbered copy that this particular municipality received. The document was distributed in numbered copies. We have exemplars of those copies, various numbers. I'm not sure whether we have 79. But my supposition would be that number 79 refers to the numbering of those documents and that is the number on the copy given to that municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I can take you to Exhibit P25, I think, which is copy 100, and Exhibit P25.1, which is copy number 93. I believe we also have another exhibit, P -- a copy which is numbered 96. Thank you. I've finished that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Ms. Sutherland. Mr. Treanor, if you turn the page over, page 2, top of the page, under VI, last part of that paragraph, instructions given by the SDS and BH. Would you say that that is also a reflection of the instructions that you have been telling us about and which appear in the preamble?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that's a very good question, Your Honour. This reference is to my mind more ambiguous.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. That's why I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Or is ambiguous. The previous reference, I think, is clear. This uses the word in the original Serbian, in the plural. In English, there's no difference between the translation of the singular of this word and the plural of this word. This uses the plural of the word, so it's the given instructions of the SDS BiH. So that reference to that particular document which uses the word in the singular is not as strong. It could be reference to a package of instructions or a number of instructions, which may or may not include the one we're discussing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honours, just so the record is clear, I gave the wrong numbers, and I would just repeat it. Exhibit P25 is copy numbered 96; P25.1 is copy number 93; and P97 is copy number 100.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And now we have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. I recognise Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just trying to find out which word he's talking about which is plural, singular.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Can he refer us to where he's referring, what paragraph, what word?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, have you followed --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's in paragraph 6. I've lost the document here. Okay. I'm putting the original on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Is it uputstva?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the word I'm referring to, uputstva. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If the witness could now be shown Exhibit P750.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This exhibit is entitled a brief and it's from the Sanski Most municipal board. If I could take you to nearer the bottom of page 3. Under paragraph B, year 1992, we can see a reference to an establishment of the war staff of the Sanski Most municipality on the 15th of January, 1992, and more intensive preparations.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm still looking for B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Page 3, supposedly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Page 3 of the English translation, subparagraph B.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. Year 1992?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Although there's no reference to the instructions, there's an establishment of the war staff of Sanski Most municipality, less than 30 days after the 19 December 1991 instructions.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could the witness now be shown --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Ms. Sutherland, because two lines below that, or if not two lines, it's one, two, three -- it says: Also establishment of the Crisis Staff and TO defence staff of Sanski Most municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So we have the use of war staff and Crisis Staff in the same context, more or less, decisions being taken. I don't know. Perhaps Mr. Treanor can enlighten us on this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, again, I'd have to study the original.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. I mean, you need to see the Serb -- the B/C/S version. When is this document dated, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It's undated, Your Honour. It is a typed document with additional handwritten notes at the back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Has it been objected to by Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It probably was, Your Honour. It's probably one of these documents that was found on the floor of the bathroom or something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Whose bathroom?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm certain I objected to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Has the witness been provided with the B/C/S version?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I've just received it. One of the problems with these documents is that the set-up of the document and the translation and the original is sometimes a bit different. Okay. Yes. The 1992 is handwritten in this document, out in the margin, and at that point it says: "Formation of a war staff of the municipality of Sanski Most, 15 January 1992, and more intensive preparations." And then two points down we have: "Formation of a Crisis Staff." And in the original here it says: "The STO, which I take to mean the Serbian Territorial Defence, of the municipality of Sanski Most." So there is reference to both the war staff and a Crisis Staff. The reference in between to the formation of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: District staffs.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- district staffs, I'm not sure what the translation is, or regional staffs or whatever - it's a different word - different route than the other words we've been seeing in connection with ARK, for instance, region and district. I take to mean on the lowest level, the level of the local community. I could be wrong about that, but that's what I take that to mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, but it makes sense, Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: May I continue, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown Exhibit P1705.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just for the record the phrase that was being used there for the local staffs is the "rejonski stabovi."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Usher, perhaps this one can be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's do that, because it's -- we are running out of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, this is a document, a decision on the establishment of the Serbian municipality of Donji Vakuf. I have the date of the document is -- of a meeting held on the 5th of February, 1992. That document -- sorry. The 15th of February, 1992. That document also makes reference to the 19 December 1991 instructions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, it has been highlighted for you, Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm having trouble finding that one. It appears to be a reference. Again, I would compare that with the original title of the document. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's using the word in the singular, the word "instructions."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown Exhibit P2489.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is a decision on the establishment of the Serbian municipality of Tuzla, adopted at a session held on the 3rd of March, 1992. Is the reference -- we can see that there's a reference to the 19 December 1991 instructions in this document?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. And finally, could you be shown a new document. And again, this document is just being disclosed at this point. It's from a municipality which falls outside of the Autonomous Region Krajina. If it could be marked P2688. This is an excerpt from a big book of minutes, and it is the minutes of the meeting of the Bratunac SDS municipal board held on the 23rd of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can I take you to paragraph 2. "The president of the board, Mr. Miroslav Deronjic opened the meeting. He told the members about the meeting of the SDS presidency in Sarajevo. He read the new material, and we moved onto the first point of the agenda." Does the meeting then discuss which variant is applicable to their municipality?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Under -- in the next numbered paragraph under that, which is -- yes, labelled 1 in the translation. As in the original, "the decision was reached to form the Serbian BiH -- the Serbian BiH, two variants, A and B, were proposed. For us, the variant B was envisaged, second level of organisation." And the word in the original for "level" is stepen, which I have been rendering as degree throughout my testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but does it read in B/C/S the equivalent of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. second degree of organisation? I want to know whether there is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The second degree of organisation or organising.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of organising. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. I've finished with that document. Could you now be shown another document, a new document. Could it be marked P2689.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This document is from the Serbian municipality of Foca Crisis Staff, dated the 25th of April, 1992. I just want to take you to the signature block in relation to the question asked by Mr. Ackerman yesterday, were you aware of any documents of -- relating to the commander of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says in this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The signature block is for the commander --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the commander of the Crisis Staff, Miroslav Stanic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. And finally, one more document --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: And there is a signature and seal on this copy of the original.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Another new document, if that could be marked Exhibit P2690. This is a document dated the 10th of May, 1992, from the Ilidza Serb municipality Crisis Staff. And again, it's in relation to the issue of commander, and if I could take you to the signature block.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you concede the point, Mr. Ackerman, we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I do. It says "commander."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Next.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And, Mr. Treanor, it's a number of documents that are referred to in the main -- the addendum report, and what you said yesterday, now I put that together with the fact that we have documentation indicating that crisis staffs were indeed in fact formed during the period between the 19th of December and the 14th of February. I put these facts together to draw the conclusion that at some point in time after the 19th of December and before the 14th of February, the local, the municipal SDS officials were in fact instructed, believed they had been instructed at least to form crisis staffs. A number of the documents that I've shown you today, are they what you based your opinion on?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had not seen before or do not recollect having seen before some of the documents you showed me today. On a quick check, they are not cited in the addendum. There are documents cited in the addendum which speak to that point which would have been basically the documents that I based my statement on. I think the additional documents you have shown me today confirm me in that statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just have a moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions for Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I have very few questions, and more or less to put my mind at rest for the future, for the exercise that we have to do in the future, since, as I explained yesterday, you are an ex parte witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, I take it that all the documents that you used in your research and in preparation of the two reports were all supplied to you by the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me -- let's explain how it works. The Office of the Prosecutor, broadly understood and understood to include myself and members of my team, acquires documents in various manners. They are submitted to the Evidence Unit, made available electronically, and myself and members of my unit use that repository of documents for our research. We identify particular documents that we want to use for particular reports on the basis of electronic searches, our knowledge of particular collections of documents, if I can use that word, for batches of documents that come in at one time, since we had been involved in their collection in the first place. And we necessarily have to make a selection of documents to -- out of the universe of documents, relevant documents, to put into a report. We do not necessarily put in every document which speaks to every point, for purposes of economy. For instance, the establishment of crisis staffs. We would not necessarily have felt it necessary to track down every document for the purpose of the addendum, every document that documented the establishment of a Crisis Staff, but merely a few examples to show that in fact it happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Let me phrase my question in a more -- directly. At one point -- before I proceed, I may require another five minutes, maximum, and then we can call it a day. Can we proceed, or do you require a break, interpreters? I can't see behind the dark windows. We can proceed. Okay. I thank you. At some point in time you were approached by the Office of the Prosecutor and asked to be their expert witness on this subject-matter.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Were you then furnished with a set of documents which you were to make use of, or were you given access to the archives of the Office of the Prosecution and given the opportunity to make the selection yourself, of which documents you would make use of?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, as a matter of fact, we're talking about both things. We have complete access to all the documents that are in the -- they're available to anybody, anybody in the office of the Prosecutor, and we certainly made use of those. I think we were also given a couple of binders of material perhaps in the vein of: "And by the way, we hear some things that -- about this municipality or something you might find it useful." But we certainly did not confine ourselves to any group of documents that was explicitly given to us for that purpose. The report is based on access to the complete collection of documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Was there at any time any request from you or your team for access to further documents which were not available at the time? Was there such a request?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any. I'm not sure what you mean by "request." In the normal course of work, there may have been - it may have been, and I can only speculate in interchange, and I'm only raising it to be complete and frank - between myself or a member of my staff and the people working on this case or another case along the lines of: By the way, do you have anything else on this? This is what we've found. It is sometimes difficult to find things in the system, as we call it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. This is why I'm asking, actually, because in the process of going through documents, you may find or you may come across information, an indication of the existence of other documents which may not be readily available, in which case I would take it that you would ask for those documents to be made available if they are available. Was there such a case or not?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you don't remember, just say you don't remember, I mean --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We frequently do ask outside entities, and to include the authorities in the states in the former Yugoslavia, to provide us with copies of particular documents of whose existence we become aware through our reading of other documents. Within the office that may also occur. Does anyone know about this? That happens rather regularly, as one of the tools of research, not simply doing electronic searches on the system and using one's memory, et cetera, but asking people who might know: Do you have anything on this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a particular case, in regard to this report, I could not bring anything to mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Did you at any time engage into any discussion with the Prosecution team in this case on the contents or merits of any of the documents that were given to you or that you were making use of?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prior to my testimony?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. In the course of your -- the course of in your investigations, research, and preparation of the report. In other words, did you sit down with any of the officers involved in this case to discuss the merits of any of the documents that had been --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes we certainly discussed the documents and I suppose it could loosely be referred to as the merits of certain documents came up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Are you aware of any other documents or sources of information that are relevant to your task which you did not ask for? You chose not to have, in other words, or not to ask for?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I just want --

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We do spend a lot of time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. I just want -- I told you. I'm not putting into doubt your integrity, Mr. Treanor. Don't misunderstand me or misread me. I just want to put on record your answers so that we would be in a better position to evaluate the weight of your two reports.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just add in that regard that there are certainly sets of documents that we do not have that I would like to have. Whether in every case a request has been made to, say, the authorities of Republic Srpska for those documents, I can't say right now. I'm thinking, for instance, just say the records of the Crisis Staff of Kotor Varos. I don't know whether we have made a specific request for those documents. I know we have made a lot of requests to the authorities of Republika Srpska, and I know that they have not responded to a lot of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. And one final but important question. In your report, did you omit, at any time, to mention or refer to events and/or documents which, if mentioned or referred to, would have either weakened the case of the Prosecution or in any way helped the accused?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, as I pointed out yesterday, I'm not a lawyer, and we don't write these reports with a copy of the indictment in any particular case at our elbow. I have to confess, I'm not particularly familiar with the details in the indictment, as it may stand now, certainly in this case. We put in the report what we believe to be relevant, within the scope of trying to keep the report to a reasonable length. If we got involved in putting in a footnote or something every document that we could possibly find on every issue, it would be a massive and unwieldy report and certain a massive and unwieldy documentary annex to the report. One of our duties is certainly to keep our eyes open for any exculpatory evidence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is what I wanted.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, we're not lawyers, but we try to do this to the best of our ability and any such document in any case we bring to the attention of the lawyers in that case. It is not necessarily done via an official report of this type. Indeed, I don't think that would be the proper format for doing that. That's all I can say on that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And my final question. I refer you to page 71, paragraph 186 of the addendum report, the part dealing with your conclusions, and particularly with Mr. Brdjanin's institutional role. And I know that this part is divided into two paragraphs. One explains the other. But I would like some further elucidation from you on the first of these paragraphs, which reads: "The available documentary evidence would not suffice to prove or to infer reasonably a scheme of systematic and mandatory implementation of all Mr. Brdjanin's enactments by the municipal bodies." Can you elaborate on that? I will also read, also for the public, the rest of what you write in paragraph 187. "Nevertheless, the available documentary evidence is more compelling in the above-mentioned critical areas: Disarmament, dismissals, resettlement, regardless of the precise state of authority of Brdjanin, his enactments were in fact implemented for these three critical purposes. In these three areas, the available documentary evidence indicates that the municipal institutions acted either directly prompted by Mr. Brdjanin or in a way concurrent and consistent with his policies." So if you take these two together, and particularly the first one, where do we stand, Mr. Treanor? Because we are judging a person here.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these two paragraphs taken together are conclusions based on the collection of documents that is available to us and that were consulted in the course of compiling this report. The first paragraph refers to documentation about all the decisions. There are 100 and some-odd decisions that we have been able to discover, and they're listed -- the documentation for their implementation in toto is -- leads Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. us to the conclusion in this paragraph, which I think is a -- we're being conservative here in our judgement there, because we do not have documentation on the implementation of a lot of those decisions. So we draw that conclusion. However, in certain areas, we seem to have better documentation, and that leads to the conclusion in paragraph 187. I would add in this connection that, in my view, and to my knowledge, the universe of documents that we have at our disposal, that is, the ones that are in possession of the Office of the Prosecutor, is not complete. I pointed that out before. And it is probably stronger in relation to the three areas mentioned in paragraph 197 -- 187 - I'm sorry - than in relation to other areas, since in the course of the years of collecting documents, documents in that area were deemed to be more significant than documents in other areas. So therefore, more of them were collected. So we're sort of -- the report is -- and what's in it is limited by the documents that are available to us. And I think I can say again safely that over the course of the years, as documents were being collected - and I don't necessarily mean to imply that there was a -- I specifically want to say that there was not a well-thought-out, planned process of doing that over the years and the documents that were collected were not necessarily collected, and probably weren't collected with a view to doing the type of analysis that we have in this section of the report. The analysis is based on such documents as I think happened to be available to us, acquired through the methods I described. What we do see, and we had a demonstration of that today, is that - and this occurs time and again - that the more documents we get, the stronger our conclusions become.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. That brings your evidence to an end. I thank you, Mr. Treanor. If there is no further business, remarks, comments, we stand adjourned until -- yes, Mr. Ackerman. Do we need to change -- stop and change the tape?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: About ten seconds, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm assuming that since the Prosecutor chose this person as an expert witness and gave him access to their complete collection via electronic searches that our expert will also be given access to that complete collection that the Prosecutor has, of documents. I'll take that up with the Prosecutor but I assume that will be the case out of fairness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I will not comment on that. First you put your request to the Prosecution and then we'll see how the Prosecution responds to that. But I see that the Prosecution doesn't agree with you. We stand adjourned until tomorrow morning at 9.00. Thank you, Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Always a pleasure.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 17th day of October 2003, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25
